sample.task: Write an episode of Hetalia where America tells his friends the story of how Big Bird almost went to space in the 1980s.
sample.chosen:
(The scene opens up in the middle of the G7 summit, with America, England, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and Canada all gathered around a table.)

America: (excitedly) Guys, you won't believe what almost happened in the 1980s!

England: (skeptical) What is it this time, America? Another one of your wacky ideas?

America: (ignoring England's comment) I was going to send Big Bird to space!

(The other countries stare at America in disbelief.)

Germany: (incredulous) You wanted to send a children's television show character to space?

America: (defensively) Hey, it wasn't just my idea! NASA was on board too!

Canada: (curious) Really? How did that even come about?

America: Well, it all started when Big Bird was invited to a space camp in Florida. He did so well that NASA approached Children's Television Workshop with the idea of sending him to space as a way to promote the space program to kids.

France: (amused) Only you, America, would think of something so absurd.

Italy: (excitedly) But what happened? Did Big Bird actually go to space?

America: (disappointed) Unfortunately, no. The plan was eventually scrapped due to safety concerns and budget cuts.

Japan: (sympathetic) That's too bad. It would have been quite the sight to see.

England: (sarcastically) Yes, I can only imagine the headlines now: "Giant yellow bird soars into the cosmos."

America: (grinning) Yeah, it would have been pretty epic.

(The other countries chuckle and shake their heads, but can't help but be amused by America's wild imagination and love for the absurd.)

(The episode ends with a shot of Big Bird looking up at the stars, dreaming of what could have been.)

Title: "The Space Mission"

America: Hey, guys! I've got a story to tell you about a time in the 1980s when we almost went to space.

Friend 1: Oh, really?

America: Yeah, I was working on a project with some other scientists, and we were trying to figure out how to send a small satellite into orbit. We had all the parts we needed, but we were missing one crucial component - a big, heavy rocket.

Friend 1: Oh, no!

America: Yeah, we were pretty close to launching, but then we realized that we didn't have enough fuel to make it to space. We tried everything we could think of, but nothing worked.

Friend 1: Wow, that's crazy!

America: Yeah, it was a disaster. We spent months working on this project, and we were pretty close to giving up. But then we remembered something - we had a friend named Big Bird who was always up for an adventure.

Friend 1: Oh, really?

America: Yeah, we asked him if he wanted to help us, and he said yes. He was a little nervous at first, but he was really excited about the challenge.

Friend 1: That's cool!

America: We spent the next few weeks trying to figure out how to make Big Bird's rocket work with ours. We finally got it working, and we launched the satellite into orbit.

Friend 1: Wow, that's amazing!

America: Yeah, it was a lot of work, but we finally made it. We were so proud of ourselves, and we knew that we had to keep working hard to achieve our goals.

Friend 1: Me too!

America: So, that's the story of how we almost went to space with Big Bird. It was a lot of fun, and we're still proud of it to this day.

individual_preference.feedback1: The response is not helpful. The prompt asks for an episode of "Hetalia" to be written. The response fails to write an episode; rather, it writes a basic dialogue between "America" and "Friend 1". In the webseries "Hetalia" the characters are all named after and represent different countries, or locations. The use of "Friend 1" would be inaccurate for this specific webseries, and the short 2 to 3 word responses do not add value. The conversation would likely happen between "America" and another character with a country name such as "Italy", "Germany", etc. The webseries "Hetalia" typically tells stories about real historical events. Given this fact, the storyline in this response is completely false and contradictory. The prompt requests the episode to tell the story of when Big Bird almost went to space. The response states in the beginning it is going to tell a story "about a time in the 1980s when we almost went to space", but then goes on to tell about trying to send a rocket to space and needing Big Bird's help. The true events took place on Jan. 28, 1986; Big Bird was asked to join a mission to orbit Earth on the Challenger to encourage kids to get interested in space. When the time came, they realized that the Big Bird costume was too big, so they decided to send a teacher instead. The mission went forward and ended up exploding and killing seven crew members.

Big Bird was unable to join the Challenger due to the costume being too big to fit inside the shuttle. Instead, a teacher was sent in Big Bird's place. The response also fails to mention that when the shuttle did take off, it exploded and 7 crew members were killed.
